title: Premium Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts

h1: Premium Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Every painter says they use good paint. This page shows how to check the actual coating system written on a bid, so the word premium means something specific.

sections.h2: Making paint quality something you can verify
body: Premium Painting is among the painting companies North Central Florida property owners may be comparing with Precision Paint Experts. We do not make claims about other contractors. What this page offers is a way to compare the coating system on any proposal, since the material and how it is applied determine how long the finish lasts.

Brand names alone tell you little. Every major manufacturer sells several tiers, and the difference between them can be substantial. What you want on paper is the exact product line for each surface, the primer, and the number of coats.

Surface condition is the other variable. The best product available will still fail on a wall that is dirty, chalky, damp, or cracked. That is why a strong spec always pairs the coating with a prep plan: washing, mildew treatment, scraping, sanding, re-caulking, and spot-priming before the first topcoat. When you compare bids, look for the prep and product together, because neither one tells the full story on its own.

sections.h2: Matching the product to the surface
body: Different substrates need different chemistry. Here is how Precision Paint Experts specifies them, using premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines:
bullets: Stucco with hairline movement: elastomeric, which flexes with the wall.
Cabinets, doors, and railings: waterborne urethane enamel for a hard, washable finish.
Exposed wood such as decks and fences: penetrating stains.
Bare or repaired spots: spot-primed before topcoat.

body: Our baseline is two full coats, with a third on dramatic color changes or porous substrates. A single heavy coat is not the same as two properly applied ones, so it is worth asking every bidder to state the number.

Application matters too. Spraying is fast, but on rough or porous surfaces the paint can bridge over texture instead of soaking in. Where penetration matters, we back-brush or back-roll sprayed surfaces. Our article on what professional exterior crews do not advertise covers more of these details, and how Florida weather affects a paint job explains why timing is part of the spec.

sections.h2: Questions that test any coating spec
body: Ask each bidder which product line goes on each surface, whether that line is named on the estimate, how many coats are included, how sprayed areas are worked in, and what warranty covers the labor as opposed to the product. On our proposals, the product line is named on the estimate, and the written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years on exterior projects sits on top of the manufacturer's product warranty.

Finally, check that the spec covers color. A deep or saturated color may need a tinted primer or an additional coat for full coverage, and that should be visible on the estimate rather than discovered halfway through the job.

sections.h2: See the spec before you decide
body: A crew lead will walk the property, take moisture readings where needed, and write an itemized estimate, usually within one business day. Explore our exterior painting or stucco repair and painting services, or request a free estimate and compare the coating system line by line.

faqs.q: Which paint brands do you use?
faqs.a: We use premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines, and the specific product line is named on every estimate.

faqs.q: Why would a job need a third coat?
faqs.a: A third coat is added on dramatic color changes or porous substrates, where two coats may not give full, even coverage.

faqs.q: Is elastomeric paint right for every stucco wall?
faqs.a: We use elastomeric on stucco with hairline movement. The walkthrough determines which coating fits each surface.
